method: jevify: judge_batch with each design's top-band screenshot plus build notes; rubrics frozen before judging. Pass 1 absolute scores (0-4), pass 2 round-robin pairwise in both orders (20 games, 8 per design).

theme.instructions: Deadlock's base game look: 1920s occult New York, art deco and pulp touches, the stock amber (#CF9943) vs sapphire (#5165AE) team colours, the game's own fonts (Reaver serif, Retail Demo, VALVE Oracle numerals) and its torn-paper/brass motifs. How strongly does this top bar read as part of that game?
criteria: Generic; could belong to any game
Indistinguishable from an official Deadlock broadcast surface

legibility.instructions: On a 1080p stream, how quickly can a viewer read the clock, both team names, the series score, and each player's state (health, ultimate ready or cooldown, dead with respawn timer)?

occlusion.instructions: How little of the gameplay view does it cover (height, opaque area, full-width bands)?

organizer.instructions: For a community tournament organizer: room and clear places for event name, stage, team names, team logos, series score; would it survive long team names and different logos?

feasibility.instructions: Using the build notes in the state, how directly can this be built in Deadlock Panorama, which supports gradients, images, borders, radii, opacity, transforms, opacity-mask images, text-shadow and radial clip arcs, but not box-shadow glows, filter blur or clip-path, and has no runtime SVG drawing?

verdict.instructions: Overall, for a community tournament observer top bar in Deadlock's own style:

criteria.shortlist: Strong on theme and legibility with no serious weakness; a top pick.
criteria.alternative: Viable, with one clear weakness or a narrower use case.
criteria.drop: A serious weakness in theme, legibility or feasibility.

winner.instructions: Two candidate observer top bars for community Deadlock tournaments, image A first then image B (each is the top 200px of a 1920x1080 match frame). Which should be built? Weigh, in order: reads as Deadlock's own base-game style; a viewer reads clock, team names, series and player state at a glance; covers little of the gameplay; fits organisers' long team names and logos.

criteria.A: Image A is the better top bar on balance.
criteria.B: Image B is the better top bar on balance.

escalation_rule: any score confidence < 0.5, verdict top p < 0.6, or verdict disagreeing with the score totals; I compare those against the screenshots myself
reading: Weak signal. Pass 1 confidences are mostly under 0.5 and every verdict is 'alternative' near 0.5, so all five escalated. Theme scores rank d2 3.17, d1 3.10, d3 3.04, d4 2.82, d5 1.99; feasibility ranks d1 first and d5 last (its trend graph). Pass 2 has d5 winning all 8 games, then d1 and d4 5, d2 2, d3 0, which conflicts with its own instruction to weigh theme first; the judge appears to reward the compact, low-occlusion bar. d1 vs d5 was a coin flip in both orders.
